subject: Interpretation of the INLA summary results for Bayesian Cox PH model

messages.author: a9dbf0805e99b82d
messages.subject: Interpretation of the INLA summary results for Bayesian Cox PH model
parts:
Hello group,
I wanted to get this clear. When implementing the Cox PH model using the survival package we exponentiate the results to get the hazards. Should we also exponentiate the mean and their Credible intervals by using exp((model$ summary.fixed)? or do we just interpret the summary(model)?
thanks,
Jerita

messages.author: da4a520efa6de5ac
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of the INLA summary results for Bayesian Cox PH model
parts:
Hi,

You can find a good explanation in the book Bayesian Regression Modeling with INLA (https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.1201/9781351165761/bayesian-regression-modeling-inla-xiaofeng-wang-yuryan-yue-julian-faraway).

And yes, you have to exponentiate the model summary. The raw output gives the treatment effect e.g. 0.5 (mean)  with 95% credible interval (0.5, 0.6). To get the posterior hazard ratio and it's 95% credible interval you have to exponentiale both of these terms. 

Best, Eva
